D001.call_notes:
Rep: Tobias, good to hear from you. Did the signed paperwork make it over okay?
Tobias Parekh (Head of HR): It did, yes, Thaddeus scanned it Tuesday, or maybe Wednesday, anyway it's in your inbox. I wanted to get on the phone before we kick off, partly to say thank you and partly because I'm a rambler and I like to explain myself.
Rep: Please. I'd love to hear what tipped it.
Tobias Parekh (Head of HR): So, honestly, we were leaning toward Corvane for a while. Everyone talks about them. But then the demo happened and I brought my list of questions, the ugly ones, like what happens when someone moves from our Texas office to Colorado mid-quarter. And you didn't flip to a slide, you just did it. Right there on the screen. Showed me the withholding change, the new state account getting picked up. I think Thaddeus actually laughed.
Thaddeus Galbraith (Payroll Manager): I did laugh. I've been burned by that exact scenario. Normally a vendor says 'great question, we'll follow up.' You didn't follow up, you answered.
Tobias Parekh (Head of HR): Right. And the other thing, and this is a smaller thing, but your implementation lady, what's her name, Odile? She sent a week by week plan before we'd even signed. Who does what, what we need from Thaddeus by when, when we run payroll in parallel. Thaddeus, you printed it out, didn't you?
Thaddeus Galbraith (Payroll Manager): It's on my wall. Two parallel runs, then we cut over on the first pay period of the month. I can actually picture it.
Tobias Parekh (Head of HR): So that's it, really. The demo felt like it was built for us and the plan felt like a plan. We have sixty-seven people, three states, and I didn't want to be somebody's guinea pig.
Rep: That means a lot. Odile will be in touch Monday to set the first working session.
Tobias Parekh (Head of HR): Perfect. Oh, and tell your demo person thanks. Sorry, I'm rambling again.

D002.call_notes:
Rep: Linnea, thanks for taking the time. I wanted to check in after the demo to see where things stand.
Linnea Galbraith (Office Manager): Of course. So, I'll be upfront. We've decided to go a different direction. We're making a change, but it's not with you, if that makes sense.
Rep: Understood. Can I ask what you're moving toward, or what shaped the decision?
Linnea Galbraith (Office Manager): Oh, it's just where we landed. Honestly it was a good conversation all around. Rafferty and I went back and forth, and then we just made the call. The team was lovely, and I mean that.
Rafferty Oyelaran (Compliance Lead): Yes, we appreciated everyone's time. It's a different direction for us. Nothing more to it than that.
Rep: I appreciate that. If there's anything we could have done differently, I'm always happy to hear it.
Linnea Galbraith (Office Manager): No, no. Really. We just made a change. I wouldn't read anything into it.
Rep: Fair enough. Sixty people, one location, so I know you've got a lot on your plate.
Linnea Galbraith (Office Manager): We do, ha. We always do. Anyway, thank you for the demo. It was thorough, and the notes you sent were tidy.
Rep: Glad they were useful. Should I keep you on the list for product updates?
Linnea Galbraith (Office Manager): Sure, that's fine. And please say thanks to your team from us.
Rafferty Oyelaran (Compliance Lead): Yes, thank you. Good luck to you all.
Rep: You too. Take care, both.
Linnea Galbraith (Office Manager): Bye now. Take care.
D002.closing_email:
Subject: Thank you

Hi Linnea,

Thank you for letting us know. We appreciated the chance to meet you and Rafferty, and we completely respect the decision to go a different direction.

It was a pleasure working with your team throughout the process, and everyone here enjoyed the conversations. We wish you and everyone at Ironbark all the best with the change.

If anything shifts down the road, or you simply have a question about anything we discussed, please do not hesitate to reach out. We would be glad to help.

Warm regards,
Your Lanternmere HR team

D003.call_notes:
Rep: Marisol, thank you for joining. I understand you have a decision to share.
Marisol Hollander (HR Generalist): Yes. I would like to be clear and fair to you. The platform itself performed well in the demonstration. Payroll, the multi-state filings, all of it was satisfactory.
Rep: I appreciate that. What was the deciding factor?
Marisol Hollander (HR Generalist): We hire constantly, and we need requisitions, candidate pipelines and offer letters in the same system as the employee record. You do not have an applicant tracking module. I asked about it twice in the demonstration, and the answer, quite properly, was that it is not offered. For us that is a requirement, not a preference.
Rep: Understood. Did you find something that does cover it?
Marisol Hollander (HR Generalist): We are looking at the options. I would add, in the interest of candour, that the project itself has also slowed. Our finance team imposed a freeze on new software spending until the new year. So even had the applicant tracking been present, I do not believe we could have signed this quarter.
Tobias Eastwood (Controller): That is correct. The freeze is a separate matter, though. The recruiting piece was the principal concern.
Rep: Thank you both. I will note that and keep you informed if we ever add it.
Marisol Hollander (HR Generalist): We would be grateful for that.

D004.call_notes:
Rep: Beatrix, thanks for jumping on. How'd the numbers shake out?
Beatrix Petrakis (Operations Manager): Not great for you, I'm afraid. I'll just say it. Your quote comes to about eleven thousand a year for eighty-seven people. That's roughly a hundred and twenty-five a head. We found another option at under seven thousand. Close to eighty a head.
Rep: Okay. Is there anything on our side we could do on the structure? Fewer modules, a different term?
Beatrix Petrakis (Operations Manager): I asked Fenella the same thing. Fenella?
Fenella Hollander (General Manager): We looked at it. Even stripped down, you were still four grand over what we budgeted. Staffing margins are thin. I can't carry that. I liked the product, I'm not going to pretend otherwise. But I run a tight ship and the cheaper one does what we need.
Beatrix Petrakis (Operations Manager): The demo was fine. Your people were responsive. It's just a number.
Rep: I hear you. Appreciate you being direct.
Beatrix Petrakis (Operations Manager): Easier that way. We've got a payroll run Friday and I'd rather not spend all week chasing this.
Rep: Understood. If your budget changes, I'm around.
Beatrix Petrakis (Operations Manager): Will do.

D005.call_notes:
Rep: Beatrix, thank you for making time. I wanted to understand where things stand.
Beatrix Whitlock (Office Manager): Certainly. I will be straightforward with you, and I hope you will not take it badly. We have started with another provider.
Rep: I appreciate you telling me. May I ask what happened?
Beatrix Whitlock (Office Manager): It is largely a matter of timing. We first spoke on a Tuesday in the spring. We asked for a demonstration, and the first slot that could be offered was nineteen days later. Nineteen days. In that interval our director, Fenella, became rather impatient. She had been promised something for the board meeting, and she could not wait.
Fenella Whitlock (Operations Director): That is accurate. I told Beatrix that I could not present a plan without a system at least in motion. So we began a trial with someone else the following week. By the time your demonstration took place, we had already loaded half our employee records elsewhere.
Beatrix Whitlock (Office Manager): And I will say the demonstration was good. It simply arrived after our momentum had gone. We were no longer in the mood to compare.
Rep: I understand. I am sorry we were not faster.
Beatrix Whitlock (Office Manager): It is no one's fault in particular. Calendars are what they are. But a week or so, I think, we could have managed.
Rep: Thank you for the candour. I will take that back to the team.
Beatrix Whitlock (Office Manager): You are very welcome.

D006.call_notes:
Rep: Mirela, congratulations on getting everyone aligned. I gather it took a while.
Mirela Okonkwo (People Operations Lead): It did, and I apologise for the long gap between our first conversation and the demonstration. We had a reorganisation, and then the holidays. I appreciate your patience.
Rep: Not at all. What helped you decide?
Mirela Okonkwo (People Operations Lead): Two things, principally. The demonstration answered the questions I had written down in advance. I had eleven. I wanted to know how a correction to a prior pay period is handled, how a late timesheet is reflected, who can see salary data. Each one was addressed in turn without any evasion. I ticked them off as we went.
Fenella Nakamura (General Manager): I will add something. I was sceptical, as I am with all software. But your support person, when we sent a question over the weekend before signing, replied within the hour. On a Sunday. That told me what the relationship would be like.
Mirela Okonkwo (People Operations Lead): Yes. That was Fenella's deciding point, I believe. We are a small team, sixty-one people on one site, and we cannot afford to wait for a ticket.
Rep: I am glad. Our implementation lead will send the schedule on Monday.
Mirela Okonkwo (People Operations Lead): Splendid. We are looking forward to it.
Fenella Nakamura (General Manager): As are we.

D007.call_notes:
Rep: Casper, thanks for the call. I heard there was news.
Casper Hollander (Operations Manager): Yes. We're going with Tallyhold. I wanted to tell you myself rather than leave you hanging.
Rep: I appreciate that. What drove it?
Casper Hollander (Operations Manager): Our broker. He's handled our benefits renewals for, what, eleven years? When he says this is the package for a company our size, I listen. He put the bundle in front of us, payroll and enrollment and renewal reporting together, and said it'd be one less thing for him to chase every October.
Rep: Did he compare it to what we showed you?
Casper Hollander (Operations Manager): He didn't need to. I trust him. Your demo was solid, I'll tell you that, I took four pages of notes. But he is the one who is on the phone with me when the carrier changes terms. Casper, you want to add anything?
Casper Jessamy (Controller): Just that it's the broker relationship. Nothing against you.
Rep: Understood. I'd rather you're well served.
Casper Hollander (Operations Manager): Appreciate it.
D007.closing_email:
Subject: Our decision

Hi,

Thank you for the time you and your team spent with us. We have decided to go with the bundle our broker recommended. He has handled our renewals for many years and we are following his advice on this one.

Please know the demo was thorough and we appreciated how quickly you answered our follow-up questions.

Best regards,
Casper Hollander
Thornfield Fabrication

D008.call_notes:
Rep: Delphine, good morning. Fifty-two people, two states, right?
Delphine Underhill (Office Manager): Right. And I'll get to the point since you asked on a Friday afternoon. We're signing.
Rep: That's great to hear. What made the difference?
Delphine Underhill (Office Manager): Speed, partly. We spoke Monday, you had a demo on the calendar for Thursday. Three days. The other vendor, Tallyhold, took two weeks just to find a time. By the time they showed up I'd already mentally moved on. Your quick turnaround told me you'd be the same when something breaks.
Emeka Ivarsson (IT Manager): I'll back that up. I'm the one who gets the calls when payroll fails. I asked about your support hours during the demo. Not a pitch, just here's the number, here's who answers. Then I tested it, I sent a dumb question Sunday night, and got a real answer Monday at eight.
Delphine Underhill (Office Manager): He did, I watched him do it.
Emeka Ivarsson (IT Manager): And the implementation plan was clear. It said what we needed to provide and when. No mystery. I've done migrations where nobody told me I owed them a file until the day before go-live.
Delphine Underhill (Office Manager): So that's the story. Quick demo, answers that matched our situation, support that's awake. I don't need more than that.
Rep: Wonderful. I'll have the paperwork over by lunch.
Delphine Underhill (Office Manager): Good. Please do. And we'd like to start the data import before the end of the month, if that's workable.
Emeka Ivarsson (IT Manager): Send me the template today and I'll have the employee file ready by Wednesday.
Rep: Done.

D009.call_notes:
Rep: Thaddeus, thanks for picking up. How are you?
Thaddeus Brannigan (Operations Manager): Tired. Year-end. Anyway, I'll save us both the time. We're going with Tallyhold.
Rep: Okay. Can you tell me what got you there?
Thaddeus Brannigan (Operations Manager): Our broker. She's the one who runs our renewals, she knows our carriers, and she brought Tallyhold in as a bundle, payroll, benefits, the lot. Put it right in front of us, here's the package. I'm not going to argue with someone who's kept our premiums from jumping the last three years.
Rep: Did you compare?
Thaddeus Brannigan (Operations Manager): Briefly. Your demo was fine. Honestly, better than fine. Casper, you were there.
Casper Thorsen (IT Manager): It was good. But the broker already had it set up.
Thaddeus Brannigan (Operations Manager): And yeah, the price on the bundle was also a little lighter. But that's not it. If she'd put you in front of us, I'd be signing with you.
Rep: I understand. I appreciate the honesty.
Thaddeus Brannigan (Operations Manager): Sorry it's not better news.

D010.call_notes:
Rep: Lucian, thanks for calling back.
Lucian Ivarsson (HR Generalist): Sure. Short version. We're not buying.
Rep: Okay. What happened?
Lucian Ivarsson (HR Generalist): Cost. Your number is around fourteen thousand a year. We're sixty-six people. That's over two hundred a head. We had maybe nine thousand set aside. The other guy came in at about one-forty a head. That fits.
Rep: Did you consider a smaller package?
Lucian Ivarsson (HR Generalist): We did. Marisol, tell him.
Marisol Quillfeather (CFO): I looked. Even the smallest tier was still above what I can approve. It isn't about whether your product is good. It's good. I just can't spend it.
Lucian Ivarsson (HR Generalist): That's it. No drama. The cheaper one does payroll and time off. That's what we need right now.
Rep: Understood. If budget changes next year, call me.
Lucian Ivarsson (HR Generalist): Will do. Thanks for being straight with us.

D011.call_notes:
Rep: Yuki, thank you for taking my call. I wanted to understand where the project stands.
Yuki Abernethy (Office Manager): Of course. I am afraid it has stalled, to be frank. We have not selected anyone. Not you, not anyone else.
Rep: I am sorry to hear it. What happened?
Yuki Abernethy (Office Manager): Our executive sponsor, the COO, had been the champion. Oriel, you can explain better than I can.
Oriel Thorsen (COO): Yes. Our board asked us to pause several initiatives for the quarter while we reconsider priorities. The payroll system is not cancelled, it is simply not first. We are focused on a client contract renewal.
Yuki Abernethy (Office Manager): I want to be clear that there was nothing wrong with your demonstration or your people. We were all quite pleased.
Oriel Thorsen (COO): The price was a bit more than we had pencilled in, I will mention, but that was not the reason. It is a matter of the calendar.
Rep: Understood. Would it be useful if I checked back in the new year?
Yuki Abernethy (Office Manager): That would be welcome. Perhaps late January.
Rep: I will put it in my diary.
D011.closing_email:
Subject: Following up on our conversation

Hi Yuki and Oriel,

Thank you both for being so open about where things stand. I completely understand that a pause on new initiatives comes from the top, and that it has nothing to do with the work we did together.

I have made a note to reach out in late January. In the meantime, I will leave the proposal and the demonstration recording in your shared folder so they are easy to find when the time comes.

With best wishes for a productive quarter,
Your Lanternmere HR team

D012.call_notes:
Rep: Casper, how's it going?
Casper Ibarra (Chief People Officer): Good, good, busy. So I wanted to call because, well, I think we're, hm, we're going to pass. And I wanted to say why because you were all so nice.
Rep: I appreciate it.
Casper Ibarra (Chief People Officer): It's the money, to be honest. I keep running the math. Fifty-three employees. Your yearly quote is, what, nine thousand and change? That's, let's see, about a hundred seventy a person. And the other company, Tallyhold, they're closer to a hundred ten. So like six thousand a year less, give or take. For a company our size that's a whole part-time salary.
Maren Parekh (Payroll Manager): I told him, I like your product better. The reports are cleaner. But I don't write the checks.
Casper Ibarra (Chief People Officer): Right, and I don't either, really, the owner does. And he looked at six grand and that was that.
Rep: Is there any room if we adjusted the plan?
Casper Ibarra (Chief People Officer): I thought about asking, honestly. But I don't think we'd get to a hundred ten. Am I wrong? Don't answer that. I think I know.
Rep: Fair enough. Thanks for the candour.

D013.call_notes:
Rep: Ravi, welcome aboard, I guess I should say. Anything before we get started on onboarding?
Ravi Galbraith (HR Generalist): Not really. I just wanted to tell you why we picked you, since you asked on the last call. Brisk version.
Rep: Please.
Ravi Galbraith (HR Generalist): We talked on a Monday. You had a demo for us Saturday, no, sorry, Friday. Within five days. Brasswick took a month to get back to us after the first call. That alone said something.
Beatrix Delacroix (Compliance Lead): And the demo answered what I'd been asking about. Three states, we have employees in all three, and I asked how new-hire reporting gets filed in each. He just walked me through it. Didn't need to call anyone.
Ravi Galbraith (HR Generalist): Yeah. I'd sent him a list of seven scenarios the night before. Edge cases, mostly. A part-timer who works in two states. A bonus paid after termination. He did all seven live.
Beatrix Delacroix (Compliance Lead): Seven. I counted.
Ravi Galbraith (HR Generalist): And your support. When I emailed with a question after the demo, I got a reply from an actual person, not a ticket number. Same day.
Beatrix Delacroix (Compliance Lead): That's what I'd want in a crunch. Filing deadlines don't wait.
Rav: Right. So that's the whole story. Fast, specific, responsive. We have seventy-nine people and I don't have time to babysit a vendor.
Rep: That's very kind. Our implementation lead will reach out today with a kickoff time.
Ravi Galbraith (HR Generalist): Perfect. Today's good.

D014.call_notes:
Rep: Soren, thanks for the call. I wanted to hear the news directly.
Soren Santangelo (VP of People): Certainly. We have selected Tallyhold. I will be specific about why, since I suspect you would like to know.
Rep: I would.
Soren Santangelo (VP of People): Our broker has managed our benefits renewals for nine years. In the proposal stage she presented a bundle, Tallyhold's payroll attached to the benefits administration she already uses, and she recommended it. She also showed that the combined cost was about eleven hundred dollars a year less than our current spend plus your quote, though I would stress that is a minor consideration.
Rep: Understood. How did the demo compare?
Soren Santangelo (VP of People): Your demonstration, held two days after our first call, was excellent. Ingrid, you had views.
Ingrid Valdivia (IT Manager): Only that your integration documentation was the clearest I saw. But the broker relationship is the deciding factor, as Soren says.
Soren Santangelo (VP of People): Precisely. The bundle was what she put in front of us.
Rep: Thank you. That is helpful to know.

D015.call_notes:
Rep: Signe, hello! How are you?
Signe Dunmore (Chief People Officer): Oh, hello, I'm well, I'm well, trying to get through a very long Thursday. How's your week?
Rep: Busy, but good. I wanted to follow up on the proposal.
Signe Dunmore (Chief People Officer): Yes, and I feel just awful, because you've been so lovely. We're not going to be able to go forward. And it's really just the budget. I'd love to be able to say it's something exciting, but it's not.
Rep: Can I ask what you're working with?
Signe Dunmore (Chief People Officer): Well, our number was about twelve thousand for the year, we're ninety-eight people so that's what, a hundred twenty-something per person, and Thaddeus found a different provider, who shall remain nameless, at about seven-five. Seventy-five hundred. Per year. For basically the same thing, he says. Thaddeus?
Thaddeus Cadogan (Payroll Manager): Basically the same on the payroll side. Maybe not as pretty. But it works.
Signe Dunmore (Chief People Officer): And when you've got a number that's four and a half thousand different, I can't sell that to the owners, you know? I just can't.
Rep: I understand completely.
Signe Dunmore (Chief People Officer): You've been wonderful, though. Really.

D016.call_notes:
Rep: Wren, thanks for making the time. I wanted to close the loop on where things landed.
Wren Parekh (VP of People): Of course, and thank you for calling rather than leaving it to email. We have decided to go a different direction.
Rep: I appreciate you telling me. I'm curious, was there a particular area where we fell short?
Wren Parekh (VP of People): No, nothing like that to point to. It's simply the direction we've chosen. I think the demonstration was very well organised, and Kwame felt the same.
Kwame Ashgrove (Finance Director): Yes, I'd agree. The materials were clear. We're making a change, and it just happens to be elsewhere.
Rep: Understood. Is there anything I can take back to the team that would be useful?
Wren Parekh (VP of People): Only our thanks. We enjoyed the process. Seventy-four people is a lot to look after, as you know, and we wanted to do right by them, and we feel good about where we are.
Rep: That's what matters.
Wren Parekh (VP of People): Exactly. So, I'll leave it there, if that's all right.
Rep: Of course. Thank you both, and best of luck.
Kwame Ashgrove (Finance Director): Same to you. Take care.

D017.call_notes:
Rep: Oriel, thank you for squeezing me in.
Oriel Oyelaran (Office Manager): Oh, of course, of course. So, um, how should I do this, I'm just going to say it. We went with someone else, and I feel bad, because I really liked your team. My dog was barking during the demo, you remember, and the rep didn't even blink.
Rep: Ha, I remember. Can I ask what led you there?
Oriel Oyelaran (Office Manager): Mostly the price, I'm sorry. Odalys has the spreadsheet, and I keep saying we can make it work, and then I look at the total. Sixty-eight employees, you were at about thirteen thousand a year, that's, what, a hundred ninety each? And the other one's at ninety-five hundred. About a hundred forty each. Odalys, is that right?
Odalys Tillbrook (Benefits Manager): That's right. Thirty-five hundred difference. We're a logistics company with small margins, so every line gets looked at twice.
Oriel Oyelaran (Office Manager): And we thought, will we miss the extras? Probably not that much? I don't know. We might. But it's a budget thing at the end of the day.
Rep: Appreciate you being open.
Oriel Oyelaran (Office Manager): Honestly, if it were up to me, I'd have picked you. But, you know.

D018.call_notes:
Rep: Beatrix, congratulations, and welcome. Tell me, how are you feeling?
Beatrix Nakamura (Chief People Officer): Relieved, honestly! Okay, so I was going to say, I wasn't sure at all at first, because Brasswick is who we've used and we know them, but then, you know, I called you on a Tuesday and the demo was that Saturday. No, Friday. Anyway, fast. Really fast. I was not expecting that from a company this size.
Rep: We try to move.
Beatrix Nakamura (Chief People Officer): And the demo, Kwame, you tell it, you were the skeptic.
Kwame Lindgren (Payroll Manager): I was. I figured it would be slides. But he opened the actual payroll register, ran a test cycle with our three-state mess, and I sat there thinking, huh, that's our setup. My questions got answered as I asked them.
Beatrix Nakamura (Chief People Officer): And then the plan, the rollout plan, it's two pages and it says who does what each week. I love a plan like that. I'm the person who forgets things, so I need it written down.
Rep: Glad it landed.
Beatrix Nakamura (Chief People Officer): It did. So that's it. Quick, real demo, clear plan. We're in.

D019.call_notes:
Rep: Fenella, thank you, and Omar, thanks for joining as well. I understand you have news.
Fenella Quillfeather (VP of People): We do. We would like to proceed with Lanternmere HR. I thought it only right to explain what persuaded us, particularly given how thoroughly Omar examined the proposal.
Omar Delacroix (VP Finance): I did. I will be candid, I came into the second call with a long list of objections. Contract terms, data export, what happens in year two. I asked each of them.
Rep: And I hope the answers were satisfactory.
Omar Delacroix (VP Finance): They were direct, which is what I wanted. I was told how the renewal works, what exporting our records would look like, and the figures were not softened. That moved me from doubtful to supportive.
Fenella Quillfeather (VP of People): For my part, I appreciated the speed. We first spoke on a Monday and the demonstration took place on the Thursday. Three days. It showed respect for our time. And the demonstration itself addressed the questions I had actually sent, not a generic tour.
Omar Delacroix (VP Finance): Fifty-four employees, one location. It is not a complicated organisation, but we are particular.
Rep: I am delighted. We will send the agreement this afternoon.
Fenella Quillfeather (VP of People): Thank you. We look forward to beginning.
D019.closing_email:
Subject: Moving forward together

Hi,

On behalf of Marlow Supply, I am pleased to confirm that we will proceed with Lanternmere HR.

The quick demonstration, and the way our finance team's questions were answered plainly, were what convinced us. Please send the agreement over and we will return it promptly.

With thanks,
Fenella Quillfeather

D020.call_notes:
Rep: Hollis, thanks for taking this.
Hollis Oyelaran (HR Director): Yeah. It's been a long week. I'll just say it. We're not signing with you.
Rep: Okay. Thanks for telling me. What was it?
Hollis Oyelaran (HR Director): Money. I wish it were more interesting. Ninety-five people. Your proposal's around sixteen thousand a year. That's, I guess, a hundred sixty-eight a head. We found a vendor at about ten-five. So a hundred and ten, roughly. It's not close.
Rep: We might have some flexibility on the first-year number.
Hollis Oyelaran (HR Director): I appreciate it, but Beatrix will tell you the same thing. Beatrix?
Beatrix Ibarra (COO): The gap is fifty-five hundred dollars a year, and it recurs. A discount in year one doesn't fix year two. We looked at it hard. You're a better fit in a few ways. I said that to Hollis. But we can't justify it right now.
Hollis Oyelaran (HR Director): So that's it. Candid, as promised.
Rep: I appreciate it.
Hollis Oyelaran (HR Director): If things change, we'll call.
D020.closing_email:
Subject: Re: Our decision

Hi,

Thanks again for the time and for being so understanding on the call. As we said, the yearly cost was more than we could take on, and we went with a lower-priced option.

Your team was great to work with.

Hollis Oyelaran
Wexcombe Software

D021.call_notes:
Rep: Marisol, thanks for jumping on.
Marisol Santangelo (Chief People Officer): Of course, of course. So I, well, I've been thinking about how to say this. It's cost. Plain and simple. I want to say it up front.
Rep: Okay, tell me more.
Marisol Santangelo (Chief People Officer): We're eighty-four employees, one location, a brewery, and our proposal from you was, I think, twelve-eight, around twelve thousand eight hundred. Then Rafferty got a quote from another outfit for about eight-five. That's, uh, four thousand three hundred less. A year. Which for us is a new fermenter payment, basically.
Rafferty Castellane (CFO): It's a new tank, yes. I couldn't make the case.
Marisol Santangelo (Chief People Officer): And, I mean, it didn't help that it took two weeks to get the demo on the calendar. Fourteen days. That's not a reason, I'm only mentioning it, it did drag. But the product, I liked it. Really.
Rep: I appreciate the honesty.
Marisol Santangelo (Chief People Officer): Well, you've been honest with us. Think about what I'd call a reasonable price and let me know. I'm kidding. Mostly.
Rep: Ha. I'll keep it in mind.

D022.call_notes:
Rep: Bram, hello! I hear good news.
Bram Dunmore (Operations Manager): Hello, hello, yes, good news, we're signing. Noor's in the room too, I'm putting you on speaker. You can hear us, yes? Okay.
Noor Abernethy (VP Finance): Hi. Hello.
Bram Dunmore (Operations Manager): I wanted to tell you the story, because it's a funny one. When our broker first mentioned you, I figured, another vendor, another pitch. But we talked on a Tuesday and by Saturday I was watching a demo. Four days. I couldn't believe it. Brasswick, our current one, takes weeks to return a phone call, so this was a different world.
Noor Abernethy (VP Finance): I'll admit I was the difficult one. I asked about the tax filing guarantee, the fee structure, what it costs to add a person midyear. Pointed questions. And they weren't dodged. The rep said, here's the number, here's the page in the contract.
Bram Dunmore (Operations Manager): She grilled him. It was glorious.
